summary: The 'Component --- Text Area' sheet reconciled with the code, so the two now agree on every value the component renders. Token flow stays repo -> Paper: where the sheet and the code disagreed, the code's value was the one drawn. Four changes. (1) The focused row's value carried a raw 14px while the two rows above bound the same value to var(--ui-text-body-md); rebound to the token. They resolve to the same number today, so nothing looked wrong and nothing would have until a brand seed moved the base size and one of three rows stayed behind. (2) Line-height was a raw 18px on 14px type -- 1.286, off the --ui-leading-* scale entirely (tight 1.25, snug 1.3). All three field texts are now bound to var(--ui-leading-snug), the role the component ships; it is 0.2px per line larger and lands the 6-row lg box on the sheet's own 128px. (3) The typed value was --ui-text-secondary; Input ships --ui-text-primary and a form holding both must not show two inks for the same thing, so the sheet now carries --ui-text-primary. (4) Two sections ADDED, for states the sheet had never drawn and a scale it had never shown: 'Text Area Sizes' (lg/md/sm at their real 128/113/105 boxes, each captioned with its type, inset and height) and 'Text Area States' (hover = border-subtle -> border-default, error = the --ui-intent-danger-fg edge with its caption, disabled = bg-sunken with text-disabled ink and no grip; focus was already drawn). The artboard is now height: fit-content rather than a guessed fixed height. Nothing in the sheet is now derived-but-undrawn, which is why textarea.doc.ts's needsDesign is down to one entry -- the character counter, which is a live-region design question rather than a value.

migration.manual: No code change -- the code was the source. The sheet now resolves its type through tokens, so a brand seed that moves the base size or the leading moves every row together, and the sizes and states a reader needs are on the sheet rather than in a doc's derivation list.
